> 天下神器，不可為也，不可執也。為者敗之，執者失之.

Chapter 28 ended with 大制不割 — the greatest cutting does not cut. Chapter 29 goes one level deeper: the knife is down, but is the hand doing anything else?

It is. It is squeezing.

Chapter 28 blocked the cut; chapter 29 blocks the squeeze. The cut divides a whole into pieces. The squeeze presses scattered differences into one lump. Different forces, same root: the refusal to let the world stay the way it is.

## 和 and 合

The distinction this chapter turns on is one character apart, and it is the axis of the whole book's social thinking.

- 和 — harmony: different things, each keeping its own nature, producing something together. 和如羹: a soup is made of water, fire, meat, salt, and it is good because they are different.
- 合 — unification: different things pressed into one, losing their separate natures. The lump.

和 produces. 合 eliminates. 道法自然 is 和: the Dao does not press anything into a single shape; it lets each thing be so of itself.

Which is why 取天下而為之 fails. It is an attempt at 合 on a scale that cannot support it.

## 吾見其不得已

> 將欲取天下而為之，吾見其不得已.

I see that he will not get it. 不得已 here is not "has no alternative" — the usual reading of that phrase — but "cannot obtain it": the thing he is after will not arrive.

The line has two readings and both work: he cannot succeed, and he has no choice but to fail. The chapter supports either.

## 神器

天下 is a 神 thing — not "divine" as sacred, but 神 in the sense of chapter 6: an unpredictable generative potential. A thing with its own arising.

> 不可為也，不可執也。為者敗之，執者失之.

Cannot be made; cannot be grasped. Whoever makes it breaks it; whoever grasps it loses it.

The failure is not incompetence. A hand that is making a thing has already imposed a shape on it; a hand that is grasping has already decided the thing will not change. Both remove the very property that made it 神.

## 或行或隨

> 故物或行或隨；或歔或吹；或強或羸；或載或隳.

Things go ahead or follow; breathe warm or blow cold; are strong or frail; are carried or collapse.

Four pairs of opposites, and 或 appears eight times: some are this way, some that way. Which is not the same as chapter 2's 相 — there, the pairs were mutually defining (long and short make each other). Here the point is distribution: the world contains both, at the same time, and you did not arrange it.

A person who wants to govern has to accept that the distribution is not his to standardize. The moment he tries, he has started squeezing.

## 去甚，去奢，去泰

> 是以聖人去甚，去奢，去泰.

Remove the extreme, remove the extravagant, remove the excessive.

Three removals, all of them about magnitude rather than direction. 甚 is going too far; 奢 is adding more than needed; 泰 is overreaching, the excess of scale.

Note what is not on the list: no virtue to acquire, no policy to implement. The instruction is entirely subtractive, and that is consistent — the failure being corrected is an addition.

## A test

Take a group you are responsible for — a team, a family, a project. Ask where you have been standardizing rather than arranging. The sign is that difference has started to feel like a problem to solve.
